metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 128. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.translated_text: The vaitānika rites have been stated; now we shall state the domestic rites.

children.text: trayaḥ pākayajñā hutā agnau hūyamānā anagnau prahutā brāhmaṇabhojane brahmaṇi hutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are three pākayajñas: those offered as oblations, which are poured into fire; those offered forth, which are without fire; and those offered in <s>brahman</s>, namely in the feeding of brahmins.
And on this point they also cite a ṛc:

children.text: yaḥ samidhā ya āhutī yo vedeneti ||
children.translated_text: 'He who with fuel, he who with oblation, he who with the Veda,' and so on.

children.text: samidham evāpi śraddadhāna ādadhanmanyeta yaja idam iti namastasmai ya āhutyā yo vedeneti vidyayā evāpyasti prītistadetatpaśyannṛṣiruvāca
children.translated_text: Even one who, full of faith, lays on fuel should think, 'This is sacrifice.' 'Reverence to him who by oblation, who by the Veda,' means by knowledge too there is satisfaction. Seeing this, the seer said:
'For the unobstructed one, for the seeker of cattle, for the heavenly one, speak the wondrous word,
sweeter than ghee and than honey,'

children.text: vaca eva ma idaṃ ghṛtācca madhunaśca svādīyo 'sti prītiḥ svādīyo 'stvityeva tad āha
children.translated_text: For me this word is sweeter than ghee and than honey; let the satisfaction be sweeter. That is what it says.

children.text: ā te agna ṛcā havirhṛdā taṣṭam bharāmasi
children.translated_text: 'To you, <s>Agni</s>, we bring with a verse the offering fashioned by the heart.

children.text: te te bhavantūkṣaṇa ṛṣabhāso vaśā uteti
children.translated_text: May these be bulls, strong bulls, and cows for you,'

children.text: eta eva ma ukṣāṇaśca ṛṣabhāśca vaśāśca bhavanti ya imaṃ svādhyāyam adhīyata iti
children.translated_text: These very bulls, strong bulls, and cows become mine, says he who studies this <s>svādhyāya</s> (recitation of one's own Veda).

children.text: yo namasā svadhvara iti namaskāreṇa vai khalvapi na vai devā namaskāramati yajño vai nama iti hi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: 'He who with reverence, performing the good rite': indeed by reverence also; for the gods do not disregard reverence. 'Reverence is sacrifice,' so indeed a brāhmaṇa text says.

children.text: atha sāyaṃ prātaḥ siddhasya haviṣyasya juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the evening and in the morning, he should offer from the prepared sacrificial food.

children.text: agnihotradevatebhyaḥ somāya vanaspataye 'gnīṣomābhyām indrāgnibhyāṃ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ dhanvantaraya indrāya viśvebhyo devebhyo brahmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: To the deities of the Agnihotra, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Vanaspatī</s>, to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to Heaven and Earth, to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to all the gods, and to <s>Brahman</s>.
With 'svāhā'; then comes the bali-offering.

children.text: etābhyaścaiva devatābhyo 'dbhya oṣadhivanaspatibhyo gṛhāya gṛhadevatābhyo vāstudevatābhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To these same deities, and to the waters, herbs, and forest trees, to the house, to the house-deities, and to the site-deities.

children.text: indrāyendrapuruṣebhyo yamāya yamapuruṣebhyo varuṇāya varuṇapuruṣebhyaḥ somāya somapuruṣebhya iti pratidiśam ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Indra</s> and the men of <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Yama</s> and the men of <s>Yama</s>, to <s>Varuṇa</s> and the men of <s>Varuṇa</s>, to <s>Soma</s> and the men of <s>Soma</s>: thus in each direction.
To <s>Brahman</s> and the men of <s>Brahman</s>: thus in the middle.

children.text: viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo divācāribhya iti divā ||
children.translated_text: To all the gods, to all beings, to those that move by day: thus by day.
To those that move by night: thus at night.
To the rakṣases: thus to the north.

children.text: svadhā pitṛbhya iti prācīnāvītī śeṣaṃ dakṣiṇā ninayet ||
children.translated_text: With 'svadhā to the ancestors,' wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he should pour the remainder down toward the south.

children.text: atha khalu yatra kva ca hoṣyantsyād iṣumātrāvaraṃ sarvataḥ sthaṇḍilam upalipyollikhya ṣaṭ lekhā udagāyatāṃ paścātprāgāyate nānāntayostisro madhye tadabhyukṣyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpyānvādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya purastāddakṣiṇataḥ paścād uttarata ityudaksaṃsthaṃ tūṣṇīṃ paryukṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Now, wherever he is going to offer, he should smear a square altar-space on every side, not less than an arrow's length, mark it with six lines, the western lines running northward and the eastern lines eastward, three in the middle not reaching the ends; having sprinkled it, established the fire, put on fuel, swept around it, and strewn grass around it to the east, south, west, and north, he silently sprinkles around it, ending in the north.
The purification of the ghee is done with the two purifiers.

children.text: apracchinnāgrāvanantargarbhau prādeśamātrau kuśau nānāntayor gṛhītvāṅguṣṭhopakaniṣṭhikābhyām uttānābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ savituṣṭvā prasava utpunāmyacchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhiriti prāg utpunāti sakṛnmantreṇa dvistūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: Taking two kuśa blades, a span long, with uncut tips and no inner shoot between them, at their two ends, with the thumb and ring-finger of upturned hands, he purifies eastward once with the mantra, 'At the impulse of <s>Savitṛ</s> I purify you with an unbroken purifier, with the rays of <s>Vasu</s>, of the sun,' and twice silently.
In ghee-oblations, the spreading of grass is optional.
So too are the two portions of ghee in pākayajñas.
And the <s>brahman</s> priest is optional, except in the sacrifice to <s>Dhanvantari</s> and in the śūlagava rite.
He should offer with '<s>Svāhā</s> to so-and-so.'

children.text: agnirindraḥ prajāpatir viśve devā brahmā ityanādeśe ||
children.translated_text: When there is no specific instruction, the deities are <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, all the gods, and <s>Brahman</s>.
The barhis, fuel, ghee, and sviṣṭakṛt offering should be single and performed at the same time.
On this point this sacrificial verse is sung:
'Having brought pākayajñas together, with one ghee and one barhis,
one should make one sviṣṭakṛt, even when the deities are different.'
The tonsure, initiation, godāna, and marriage are to be performed during the northern course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious lunar mansion.
Some hold marriage to be suitable at all times.
Before these rites he should offer four ghee-oblations.

children.text: agna āyūṃsi pavasa iti tisṛbhiḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanya iti ca ||
children.translated_text: With the three verses beginning 'O <s>Agni</s>, purify the life-spans,' and also with 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you.'
Or with the vyāhṛtis.
Some prescribe a combination.
Others prescribe none at all.

children.text: tvam aryamā bhavasi yat kanīnāmiti vivāhe caturthīm ||
children.translated_text: At a marriage, the fourth oblation is with 'You become <s>Aryaman</s> for the maidens.'

children.text: kulam agre parīkṣeta ye mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaś ca iti yathoktaṃ purastāt ||
children.translated_text: First one should examine the family, both on the mother's and on the father's side, as stated before.
One should give a daughter to an intelligent man.
He should marry a girl endowed with intelligence, beauty, character, and auspicious marks, and free from disease.

children.text: durvijñeyāni lakṣaṇāny aṣṭau piṇḍān kṛtvā ṛtam agre prathamaṃ jajña ṛte satyam pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: The marks are hard to know. Having made eight lumps, he recites: 'Truth was born first in the beginning; in truth is the real established.

children.text: yad iyaṃ kumāry abhijātā tad iyam iha pratipadyatām
children.translated_text: Whatever this maiden has been born to, let her attain that here.

children.text: yat satyaṃ tad dṛśyatām iti piṇḍān abhimantrya kumārīṃ brūyād eṣām ekam gṛhāṇeti ||
children.translated_text: Let what is true be seen.' Having consecrated the lumps, he should say to the maiden, 'Take one of these.'

children.text: kṣetrāc ced ubhayataḥsasyād gṛhṇīyād annavaty asyāḥ prajā bhaviṣyatīti vidyād goṣṭhāt paśumatī vedipurīṣād brahmavarcasviny avidāsino hradāt sarvasampannā devanāt kitavī catuṣpathād dvipravrājinīriṇād adhanyā śmaśānāt patighnī ||
children.translated_text: If she takes one from a field bearing crops on both sides, he should know that her offspring will be rich in food; from a cow-pen, rich in cattle; from the sacrificial ground's dung, rich in sacred brilliance; from a pool not used by slaves, fully endowed with all things; from a gambling-place, a gambler; from a crossroads, twice given to wandering; from barren ground, unlucky; from a cremation ground, one who kills her husband.

children.text: alaṃkṛtya kanyām udakapūrvāṃ dadyād eṣa brāhmo vivāhas tasyāṃ jāto dvādaśāvarān dvādaśa parān punāty ubhayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having adorned the girl, he should give her with water poured first. This is the brāhma marriage; a son born from her purifies twelve ancestors and twelve descendants on both sides.

children.text: ṛtvije vitate karmaṇi dadyād alaṃkṛtya sa daivo daśāvarān daśa parān punāty ubhayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, after adorning her, he gives her to an officiating priest while the rite is under way, that is the daiva marriage; it purifies ten ancestors and ten descendants on both sides.

children.text: saha dharmaṃ carata iti prājāpatyo 'ṣṭāvarān aṣṭa parān punāty ubhayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The prājāpatya marriage is with the words, 'Practice dharma together'; it purifies eight ancestors and eight descendants on both sides.

children.text: gomithunaṃ dattvopayaccheta sa ārṣaḥ saptāvarān sapta parān punāty ubhayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, after giving a pair of cattle, he marries her, that is the ārṣa marriage; it purifies seven lower and seven higher ancestors on both sides.
If, after making a mutual agreement, he marries her, that is the gāndharva marriage.
If, after satisfying her family with wealth, he marries her, that is the āsura marriage.
If he carries her off while they are asleep or heedless, that is the paiśāca marriage.

children.text: hatvā bhittvā ca śīrṣāṇi rudatīṃ rudadbhyo haret sa rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, having killed and broken heads, he carries away the weeping girl from those who are weeping, that is the rākṣasa marriage.

children.text: atha khalūccāvacā janapadadharmā grāmadharmāś ca tān vivāhe pratīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, indeed, the customs of countries and of villages are various, high and low; one should observe them in marriage.
But what is common to all, that we shall state.

children.text: paścād agner dṛṣadam aśmānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyottarapurastād udakumbhaṃ samanvārabdhāyāṃ hutvā tiṣṭhan pratyaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukhyā āsīnāyā gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastam ity aṅguṣṭham eva gṛhṇīyād yadi kāmayīta pumāṃsa eva me putrā jāyerann iti ||
children.translated_text: Having set a flat stone behind the fire and a water jar to the north-east, when she has taken hold of him, he should offer oblations; then, standing and facing west, while she sits facing east, he should take just her thumb with 'I take your hand for good fortune,' if he wishes, 'May only male sons be born to me.'
If he desires a female child, he should take just the fingers.
If he desires both, he should take the hand together with the thumb at the tips of the hair.

children.text: pradakṣiṇam agnim udakumbhaṃ ca triḥ pariṇayaṃ japaty amo 'ham asmi sā tvaṃ sā tvam asy amo 'ham
children.translated_text: Leading her three times clockwise around the fire and the water jar, he recites: 'I am he; you are she. You are she; I am he.

children.text: dyaur ahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ sāmāhaṃ ṛk tvam
children.translated_text: I am heaven; you are earth. I am the <s>Sāman</s>; you are the <s>Ṛc</s>.
Come, let us two marry; let us beget offspring.

children.text: sampriyau rociṣṇū sumanasyamānau jīveva śaradaḥ śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: Loving each other, shining, and well-minded, let us live a hundred autumns.'

children.text: pariṇīya pariṇīyāśmānam ārohayatīmam aśmānam ārohāśmeva tvaṃ sthirā bhava
children.translated_text: After each circumambulation he makes her mount the stone: 'Mount this stone; like a stone be firm.
Withstand those who attack; stand over those who contend against you.'

children.text: vadhvañjalā upastīrya bhrātā bhrātṛsthāno vā dvir lājān āvapati ||
children.translated_text: The bride's brother, or one who stands in the place of a brother, strews twice the fried grain into her joined hands, after spreading it beneath.
For the descendants of <s>Jamadagni</s>, three times.
Having sprinkled the oblation with ghee.
And also the cut-off portion.
This is the rule for the portions cut off.

children.text: aryamaṇaṃ nu devaṃ kanyā agnim ayakṣata
children.translated_text: 'The maidens have now worshipped the god <s>Aryaman</s>, the fire.

children.text: sa imāṃ devo 'ryamā preto muñcātu nāmutaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: May this god <s>Aryaman</s> release her from here, not from there. Svāhā.'

children.text: varuṇaṃ nu devaṃ kanyā agnim ayakṣata
children.translated_text: 'The maidens have now worshipped the god <s>Varuṇa</s>, the fire.

children.text: sa imāṃ devo varuṇaḥ preto muñcātu nāmutaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: May this god <s>Varuṇa</s> release her from here, not from there. Svāhā.'

children.text: pūṣaṇaṃ nu devaṃ kanyā agnim ayakṣata
children.translated_text: 'The maidens have now worshipped the god <s>Pūṣan</s>, the fire.

children.text: sa imāṃ devaḥ pūṣā preto muñcātu nāmutaḥ svāhety avicchindaty añjaliṃ sruceva juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: May this god <s>Pūṣan</s> release her from here, not from there. Svāhā.' Without separating her joined hands, he should offer as with a ladle.
Without circumambulating, with the hollow of a winnowing basket, facing himself, he offers the fourth silently.

children.text: opyopya haike lājān pariṇayanti tathottame āhutī na saṃnipatataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some, after repeatedly pouring in the fried grain, lead her around; in that case the last two oblations do not coincide.

children.text: athāsyai śikhe vimuñcati yadi kṛte bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: Then he loosens her topknot, if the two have been made,
that is, if two woolen tufts have been tied at the two sides of the hair.

children.text: pra tvā muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśād iti ||
children.translated_text: With 'I release you from the fetter of <s>Varuṇa</s>.'
He performs the following act with the following verse.

children.text: athainām aparājitāyāṃ diśi sapta padāny abhyutkrāmayatīṣa ekapady ūrje dvipadī rāyaspoṣāya tripadī māyobhavyāya catuṣpadī prajābhyaḥ pañcapady ṛtubhyaḥ ṣaṭpadī sakhā saptapadī bhava sā mām anuvratā bhava
children.translated_text: Then, in the unconquered direction, he makes her take seven steps forward: 'For nourishment you are one-stepped; for vigor two-stepped; for increase of wealth three-stepped; for welfare four-stepped; for offspring five-stepped; for the seasons six-stepped. Be my friend, seven-stepped; be devoted to me.

children.text: putrān vindāvahai bahūṃs te santu jaradaṣṭaya iti ||
children.translated_text: Let us obtain sons; may they be many and live to old age.'
Placing both their heads together, he sprinkles them with the water jar.

children.text: brāhmaṇyāś ca vṛddhāyā jīvapatyā jīvaprajāyā agāra etāṃ rātriṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: She should spend that night in the house of an old brāhmaṇī whose husband and children are alive.

children.text: dhruvam arundhatīṃ saptarṣīn iti dṛṣṭvā vācaṃ visṛjeta jīvapatnī prajāṃ vindeyeti ||
children.translated_text: After seeing <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Arundhatī</s>, and the Seven Seers, he should release speech with, 'May I, with my wife living, obtain offspring.'

children.text: prayāṇa upapadyamāne pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyeti yānam ārohayet ||
children.translated_text: When the departure is taking place, he should make her mount the vehicle with 'May <s>Pūṣan</s> lead you from here, holding your hand.'

children.text: aśmanvatī rīyate saṃrabhadhvam ity ardharcena nāvam ārohayet ||
children.translated_text: With the half-verse 'The stony stream flows; take hold together,' he should make her board the boat.
He should make her step out on the northern side.
When she is crying, he says, 'They cry for the living.'
They carry the marriage fire in front, unceasingly.

children.text: kalyāṇeṣu deśavṛkṣacatuṣpatheṣu mā vidan paripanthina iti japet ||
children.translated_text: At auspicious places, country trees, and crossroads, he should recite, 'May the waylayers not find us.'

children.text: vāse vāse sumaṅgalīr iyaṃ vadhūr itīkṣakān īkṣeta ||
children.translated_text: At each stopping place he should have the onlookers look at her with, 'This bride is highly auspicious.'

children.text: iha priyaṃ prajayā te samṛdhyatām iti gṛhaṃ praveśayet ||
children.translated_text: He should make her enter the house with, 'Here may what is dear to you prosper together with offspring.'

children.text: vivāhāgnim upasamādhāya paścād asyānaḍuhaṃ carmāstīrya prāggrīvam uttaraloma tasminn upaviṣṭāyāṃ samanvārabdhāyām ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatir iti catasṛbhiḥ pratyṛcaṃ hutvā samañjantu viśve devā iti dadhnaḥ prāśya pratiprayacched ājyaśeṣeṇa vānakti hṛdaye ||
children.translated_text: Having set down the marriage fire, he spreads behind it the hide of a bull, with its neck toward the east and hair upward; when she has sat on it and has taken hold of him, he offers with the four verses beginning 'May <s>Prajāpati</s> generate offspring for us,' one oblation for each verse; then, with 'May all the gods unite,' he tastes curds and gives them back to her, or he anoints her heart with the remainder of the ghee.

children.text: ata ūrdhvam akṣārālavaṇāśinau brahmacāriṇāvalaṃkurvāṇāvadhaḥśāyinau syātām trirātraṃ dvādaśarātram ||
children.translated_text: From then onward the two should eat no pungent or salty food, observe chastity, wear ornaments, and sleep on the ground for three nights, or for twelve nights.
Or for a year, according to some, because a seer is born.
When he has completed the vow, he should give the bride's garment to one who knows the Sūryā hymn.
And food to brāhmaṇas.
Then he should have blessings for well-being pronounced.

children.text: pāṇigrahaṇādi gṛhyaṃ paricaret svayaṃ patny api vā putraḥ kumāry antevāsī vā ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with the taking of the hand, one should himself perform the domestic rite, or his wife, or a son, daughter, or pupil may do so.
He should be constantly favored by it.

children.text: yadi tūpaśāmyet patny upavased ity eke ||
children.translated_text: But if it should go out, some say that the wife should fast.
Its times for kindling and for offering are explained by the Agnihotra.
And what is to be offered is fit for oblation, excluding meat.
But, if desired, he may use rice, barley, and sesame.

children.text: agnaye svāheti sāyaṃ juhuyāt sūryāya svāheti prātas tūṣṇīṃ dvitīye ubhayatra ||
children.translated_text: In the evening he should offer with 'Svāhā to <s>Agni</s>'; in the morning, with 'Svāhā to <s>Sūrya</s>.' In both cases the second oblation is silent.
In the Upaniṣad are taught the rites for conception, for begetting a male child, and for preventing miscarriage.

children.text: yadi nādhīyāt tṛtīye garbhamāse tiṣyeṇopoṣitāyāḥ sarūpavatsāyā gor dadhani dvau dvau tu māṣau yavaṃ ca dadhi prasṛtena prāśayet ||
children.translated_text: If she has not studied, in the third month of pregnancy, under <s>Tiṣya</s>, after she has fasted, he should make her eat, in the curd of a cow with a calf of the same color, two and two māṣas and barley, together with a prasṛta of curd.

children.text: kiṃ pibasi kiṃ pibasīti pṛṣṭā puṃsavanaṃ puṃsavanam iti triḥ pratijānīyāt ||
children.translated_text: When asked, 'What are you drinking? What are you drinking?' she should answer three times, '<s>Puṃsavana</s>, <s>puṃsavana</s>.'
In this way, three prasṛtas.

children.text: athāsyai maṇḍalāgāracchāyāyāṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ nāsikāyām ajītām oṣadhīṃ nastaḥ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the shade of a round building, he places the unconquered herb in her right nostril.
Some say with the two formulas beginning 'possessing offspring' and 'having living sons.'

children.text: prājāpatyasya sthālīpākasya hutvā hṛdayadeśam asyā ālabheta ||
children.translated_text: Having offered from the prājāpatya cooked oblation, he should touch her in the region of the heart.
In the sixth month is the first feeding of solid food.
Goat's flesh, for one who desires the eating of food.
Partridge meat, for one who desires sacred brilliance.
Rice cooked with ghee, for one who desires vigor.

children.text: dadhimadhughṛtamiśram annaṃ prāśayed annapate 'nnasya no dehy anamīvasya śuṣmiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He should make the child eat food mixed with curd, honey, and ghee, saying, 'O lord of food, give us food that is free from sickness and strong;

children.text: pra pradātāraṃ tāriṣa ūrjaṃ no dhehi dvipade catuṣpada iti ||
children.translated_text: carry the giver forward; place nourishment in us, for two-footed and four-footed beings.'
The same procedure applies for a girl.
